title: Suspending and Terminating Construction Contracts 2026: When Allowed?
desc: When a construction contract may be suspended or unilaterally terminated in 2026: contractor abandonment, late payment, 28-day notice, liquidation in 56 days.
summary: The cases in which a construction contract may be suspended, cancelled, or unilaterally terminated under the Construction Law 2025, Decree 210/2026/ND-CP and the Civil Code, with notice and liquidation procedures.
body: p

A contractor abandoning a project half-finished or a homeowner ceasing payment is not uncommon. Suspending or terminating a contract without proper grounds can make you the party in breach. Below are the rules under Article 85 of the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP.
h2
1. When may a contract be suspended?
p
The contract must state the cases in which suspension is allowed, and the period and procedure for suspension. Suspension applies when (Clause 1, Article 85):
ul
One party seriously breaches its contractual obligations.
A force majeure event occurs (Clause 1, Article 13).
A competent state authority so requires.
A change in the law directly affects performance of the contract.
p

Public investment and PPP projects also have specific rules: the contractor may suspend if the employer is more than 28 days late in payment; the notice period for suspension is at most 28 days (Clause 2, Article 26).
h2
2. Serious breach: grounds for termination
p
Under Clause 2, Article 27 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP, the cases in which the injured party has the right to cancel or unilaterally terminate the contract are:
ol
One party assigns the contract to another person without the other party's consent.
The contractor refuses to perform or fails to perform work for 56 consecutive days, seriously affecting the schedule (unless otherwise agreed).
Work is stopped for more than 56 consecutive days through the employer's fault, without a legitimate reason.
The employer fails to pay for more than 56 days after the payment due date (unless otherwise agreed).
Other breaches as agreed or provided by law.
p

In addition, termination may also take place where force majeure means the contract cannot be amended, or where work is suspended for longer than the period in the contract through no fault of the other party (Clause 2, Article 85 of the Construction Law).
h2
3. Procedure: written notice is required
ul
The party suspending or terminating must give prior written notice stating the reasons, the time, and the legal consequences, except in force majeure (Clause 3, Article 85).
The notice period for termination is 28 days, unless the parties agree otherwise (Clause 5, Article 27).
Failing to give notice and causing damage requires compensation.
h2
4. What if termination lacks proper grounds?
p

A party that suspends, unilaterally terminates, or cancels the contract unlawfully must compensate the other party for damage (Clause 4, Article 85). If there are no grounds for termination and a party simply stops performing, it is treated as being in breach and must still continue to perform its obligations (Clause 3, Article 27; Clause 5, Article 428 of the Civil Code).
h2
5. After termination: payment, leaving the site, liquidation
ul
The contract ends from the time the other party receives the notice; the party that has performed its obligations may demand payment for the work done (Clause 3, Article 428 of the Civil Code).
The contractor removes materials and machinery from the site within the agreed time; if they cannot agree, the homeowner decides the time (Clause 6, Article 27).
The parties complete liquidation within the agreed time but no more than 56 days from the date of the termination notice, unless otherwise agreed (Clause 7, Article 27).
h2
6. Advice for homeowners
ol
State clearly in the contract the cases for suspension and termination and the notice periods.
When the contractor is late, send a written request to remedy within a reasonable time before terminating (Article 424 of the Civil Code).
Prepare a record of the site condition and the quantities completed before handing over to another contractor.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The 56-day and 28-day periods apply where the contract has no other agreement. Contracts signed before 1 July 2026 are governed by the rules in force at signing; the parties may agree to apply Decree 210/2026/ND-CP (Clause 2, Article 33).
